correctness.rationale: Every graph-theoretic premise is explicit: two capped pentagons and 30 edges, all degrees five. Fewer than six starting blue vertices cannot finish because a five-set can make only one force, ending in a closed neighborhood whose five neighbors induce a cycle and retain two white neighbors each. For every 6-set, a fully enumerated 18-orbit partition of the 924 subsets under all 120 automorphisms proves that and only that edge counts 8 or 9 are forcing, with orbit sizes 60, 20, 120 and representative forcing sequences in RESULT.md. Parallel and sequential algorithms agree on all 4096 initial sets. Full pairwise Hamming comparisons and BFS from every optimal set verify 1320 exchange edges and the distance distribution; all are reproduced by verify.py. Limits are fixed finite graphs only.

Named-object, invariant, equivalent-count, and stored-claim queries did not locate coverage. This is best-knowledge originality, not globally certified uniqueness.

value.rationale: The icosahedron is the canonical five-regular Platonic graph, a natural test for local coloring-control dynamics. Rather than an arbitrary table, the result gives an iff internal-edge criterion for every optimum, a complete polynomial for all initial-set sizes, a three-orbit structural classification with different forcing times, and a connected 200-state reconfiguration graph with exact diameter and distances. These distinguish optimal configurations and quantify optimality-preserving transformations in a motif of high graph symmetry. It is a meaningful finite self-contained classification, without claiming an infinite-family theorem.
